title: Gyroscopes
alt: We didn't actually land on the moon -- it just looked like we did because of precession.  Also, gyroscopes caused 9/11.
transcript:
[Cueball sits at a desk with a gyroscope in his hands. Text on top of the frame:]
Despite years of studying physics, I still find gyroscopes a little freaky.
[Cueball starts the gyroscope.]
Gyroscope: zzzzip

[The gyroscope spins.]
Gyroscope: zzzzzz

[Frameless panel, the gyroscope lifts into the air.]

[The gyroscope moves away from Cueball, still spinning.]
Gyroscope: GREETINGS, HUMAN.
explanation:
Cueball is playing with a . Even though he has studied them and intellectually understands their behaviour, they still seem somewhat mysterious, which is a reasonable thought. Gyroscopes hold kinetic and angular momentum at a near constant, which allows them to continuously spin for extended periods of time. At the end of the comic however, the gyroscope is revealed to have the power of levitation and to talk with him, revealing that Cueball's gyroscope is actually a sentient lifeform, turning his previously irrational apprehension into quite the understatement. How the gyroscope is able to do this is unclear. This behavior could be specific to Cueball's gyroscope, or it could be that all gyroscopes have this property, and that only this one shows it. Alternatively, their properties could be unknown because no one who has seen them are left alive to tell the story. 

In the title text, Randall is mocking the  and refers to the  in process. Gyroscopes and the lunar orbit both exhibit precession, a physical concept that non-scientists can find hard to grasp. Thus, it is a perfect subject for a lunar conspiracy theory. He goes on to claim that gyroscopes (which form part of the navigation system of every commercial airplane) were directly responsible for the 9/11 terrorist attacks.
